source_document.body:
The Salar de Uyuni, in Bolivia, is the world’s largest salt flat and is believed to hold more than 20% of the world's lithium resources. (Stock image by Sharon Jones.)
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 23, 2026
Global lithium demand is expected to more than triple by 2050, equivalent to the output of 134 new mines and more than $100 billion (C$139.8 billion) in investment before accounting for recycling, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
The London-based research firm forecasts consumption will climb to nearly 7 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) by mid-century from 2.11 million tonnes this year. At an average production capacity of 36,000 tonnes annually, the additional supply would require the equivalent of one new mine every two months over the next 24 years.
“The biggest challenge is sustaining that investment through price cycles, while competing for capital with AI, defence and the wider energy transition,” Cameron Perks, Benchmark’s product director for lithium, said in a statement.
The forecast highlights the scale of the mining industry’s challenge as governments push to electrify transportation and develop domestic battery supply chains. Financing constraints, lengthy permitting processes and competition for investment could complicate efforts to bring enough production online, particularly in Western markets seeking to reduce dependence on China.
Electric vehicles are expected to account for 76% of lithium demand by 2050, compared with 55% today. Batteries already represent 92% of consumption, up from about 70% in 2020.
Demand from stationary energy storage has expanded by more than 60% annually over the past two years, although Benchmark expects growth to moderate to about 5% a year through the end of the decade.
Supply shifts
Australia, the world’s largest lithium mining jurisdiction, is expected to account for 29% of global mined supply this year, but its share could decline to 20% by 2050 as existing operations are mined out and competing regions expand production.
The projection includes major brownfield developments such as PLS’s P2000 expansion, expected to begin around 2030.
“Many of Australia’s mines will be depleting by 2050. Price volatility has made financiers hesitant, and the regulatory burden is growing,” Perks said. “It’s not too late, but if Australia doesn’t back growth, other regions will take that share.”
China is expected to maintain roughly a quarter of global mined production, supported by continued investment in domestic resources and its established position in the battery supply chain.
North America, meanwhile, could increase its share of mined lithium output to 13% by 2050 from just 1.7% this year. The region’s portion of global lithium demand from battery cell manufacturing is forecast to double to 12% over that period.
Europe faces a similar supply challenge. Although the continent accounts for 7% of lithium demand from cell production, it contributes less than 1% of mined supply. Benchmark expects European mining output to reach 5.5% of the global total by 2050, still below its projected 8% share of cell manufacturing demand.
Developing new mines in both regions will be difficult, however, because some promising deposits require unproven technologies or face environmental and community opposition.
“These aren’t insurmountable, but they create significant delays, and they mean mines built in these regions simply cost more,” Perks said.
Recycling uncertainty
Benchmark’s outlook could prove conservative if government policies supporting electric vehicles and energy storage drive stronger-than-expected consumption.
Under its upside scenario, lithium demand could approach 9 million tonnes LCE by 2050, requiring the equivalent of around 180 new mines and more than $150 billion in investment.
Recycling offers the largest potential offset to new mining requirements. Benchmark expects recovered material to account for almost half of lithium supply by mid-century, although that projection depends on sufficient volumes of used batteries becoming available and recycling remaining commercially competitive.
Its capital expenditure analysis, which assumes recycling meets a substantial portion of future demand, estimates that about $64 billion will be needed to satisfy lithium requirements through 2040.
The timing of battery retirements remains a major uncertainty because materials cannot be recovered until batteries reach the end of their useful lives.
“Recycling will grow, but our base case asks a lot of it,” Perks said. “It’s limited by how quickly batteries reach end of life, and it still needs to compete with mines on cost. Every tonne that recycling doesn’t deliver has to come from a mine.”
The industry’s ability to finance new projects through volatile commodity cycles, while scaling up recycling capacity, will ultimately determine whether production can keep pace with the energy transition.

Cuajone copper mine in Peru. ( Image courtesy of Fluor. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 23, 2026
Southern Copper (NYSE, BVL: SCCO) is evaluating a $680-million (C$950.6 million) expansion of its Cuajone mine in southern Peru to counter declining ore grades and improve efficiency as the copper industry faces growing pressure to develop new supply.
The proposal would increase milling capacity by 33% to 120,000 tonnes per day from 90,000, with the expansion projected to produce an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually. The company is also studying a further increase to 150,000 tonnes per day.
“There’s real scarcity of supply,” Anglo American CEO Duncan Wanblad said at a mining conference last week . He pointed to limited resources, lengthy permitting processes and rising development costs as obstacles to expanding copper production.
Analysts have highlighted in recent weeks the disconnect between potential mine expansions and production that companies have committed to deliver. BloombergNEF (BNEF) estimates the industry needs $332 billion in new mine investment to avert a supply shortage likely to begin in 2028. The researchers expect the deficit to widen to 3 million tonnes, or 8% of consumption, by 2035, before reaching 20 million tonnes, or 44%, by 2050.
Geopolitics, AI demand
Adding to those concerns, geopolitical disruptions and soaring electricity demand driven by artificial intelligence (AI) are putting increasing pressure on global metals supplies, particularly copper, as mining investment struggles to keep pace, Wood Mackenzie said in a report Thursday .
Southern Copper’s Cuajone proposal underscores the challenge of turning potential capacity into actual supply. The company has outlined preliminary production targets but has yet to announce a final investment decision or timetable, leaving the project’s contribution to future output uncertain.
The company expects to decide on the scale of the expansion in early 2027, with the 120,000-tonne-per-day option currently considered more likely, CFO Raul Jacob said during Thursday’s earnings call.
Shares in Southern Copper were down slightly to $183.28 apiece in New York on Friday morning, for a market capitalization of $154.7 billion. The stock has traded in a 12-month range of $ 119.25 to $ 223.88.
Production pressures
Southern Copper’s red metal production fell 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, largely because of lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines, according to its third-quarter results released Oct. 20 .
Cuajone produced nearly 163,000 tonnes of fine copper in 2025. Together with the nearby Toquepala operation, it remains central to Southern Copper’s Peruvian business. Both mines received The Copper Mark accreditation last year for meeting sustainability standards, including requirements related to tailings management.
The company has forecast copper production of 911,400 tonnes in 2026 and about 900,000 tonnes in 2027, compared with 954,270 tonnes in 2025. Its longer-term ambition is to lift annual output to 1.6 million tonnes by 2033, supported by investments across Peru and Mexico.
Permitting progress
Southern Copper’s $1.8-billion Tia Maria project, also in Peru, is advancing after a permitting dispute earlier this year. In April, the energy and mines ministry reinstated its exploitation licence after briefly revoking the authorization and ordering a technical review amid political turmoil surrounding the presidential election.
Tia Maria was 49.6% complete as of Sept. 30, with $884.3 million invested and another $1.1 billion committed to contracts and related activities. The company expects the mine to begin operating in the first half of 2028, producing 120,000 tonnes of copper cathodes annually in its early years.
Southern Copper’s wider capital investment program exceeds $15 billion this decade, including more than $10.3 billion potentially directed towards Peruvian projects. Its development pipeline includes Los Chancas, where production is targeted for 2031, and Michiquillay, scheduled to begin operations in 2032.

Volvo expects the EX60 to become one of its best-selling vehicles ever, with over 50,000 orders already in Europe. But as demand builds, Volvo is struggling to ramp up production.
Volvo EX60 orders top 50,000 as production lags behind
After reporting third-quarter earnings on Friday, Volvo said the EX60 has been “a big success” so far, receiving over 50,000 orders in Europe since production began in April.
However, the company has built only around 5,000 units so far because of “new industrial technology,” Volvo said, such as the EX60’s cell-to-body structural battery design and manufacturing changes required for its new SPA3 platform.
The Swedish automaker admitted that the production ramp-up is “taking longer than planned,” but promised volumes are steadily improving.

Volvo Car’s president and CEO Håkan Samuelsson said the EX60 will be a cornerstone of Volvo’s comeback plan as one of its most profitable models, but warned that the financial impacts will not be realized until volume picks up.
After delivering the first models in Europe this summer, Volvo planned to ramp up production as the EX60 arrived in new markets, including the US.
Volvo EX60 orders reach over 50,000 in Europe (Source: Volvo Cars Q3 2026 earnings)
Volvo initially expected to sell about 7,000 EX60s in the US by the end of 2026, but a dealer told Automotive News last week that the company is on pace to deliver just a fraction of that.
In a note sent to dealers in late September, Volvo said it had delayed customer deliveries in the US. A company spokesperson confirmed that EX60 availability will “remain limited” in the short term. In early 2027, Volvo expects to distribute significantly more inventory to dealers.
The delay comes at a crucial point as Volvo aims to lower its break-even point and improve cash flow as part of its turnaround plan.
2027 Volvo EX60 (Source: Volvo)
As part of the restructuring, Volvo is cutting about 2,500 jobs globally, 2,000 of which are based in Sweden.
Volvo posted a loss of SEK -3.7 billion ($373 million) in the third quarter, with its operating profit margin falling to -5.6%.
“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalization, hypercompetition and climate change,” Samuelsson said. He added, “In the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions.”
Electrek’s Take
While Volvo struggles to ramp up production, other luxury brands, such as BMW, are also seeing early success with their next-generation electric vehicles.
The iX3, based on BMW’s Neue Klasse platform, received over 100,000 orders after it went on sale in October 2025.
BMW recently added a third shift at its new manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary, just months after it introduced a second shift as it ramps up output.
Volvo is betting on its new SPA3 platform to lower production costs, boost profit margins, and accelerate its push into software-defined vehicles.
As part of its turnaround plan, Volvo is working on its largest-ever product push. The plans include 13 new cars through the end of 2030.

After cardiac safety signals led to a full clinical hold on Aardvark Therapeutics’ studies of ARD-101, the biotech conducted an additional safety study, in which no cardiac events were detected. Aardvark plans to resume testing the candidate next year.
The FDA has lifted its clinical hold on Aardvark Therapeutics’ small-molecule drug candidate ARD-101, being developed for the treatment of extreme, insatiable hunger in Prader-Willi syndrome, after a new study in healthy volunteers revealed no cardiac events.
Aardvark voluntarily suspended the Phase 3 HERO and open-label extension (OLE) studies of ARD-101 in February, pointing to “reversible cardiac observations.” These signals were detected during a routine safety check in a healthy volunteer study, and occurred in participants who were given the investigational therapy at above-therapeutic doses.
With the regulatory pause removed, Aardvark plans to resume testing ARD-101 in Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS), the biotech said in a Thursday announcement .
“The Company plans to request a meeting with the FDA to align on Phase 3 plans for ARD-101 and expects to resume PWS clinical activities in 2027,” a company spokesperson confirmed to BioSpace over email, but did not provide specific details about the late-stage program.
Patients who were treated with a 1,600-mg dose of ARD-101 twice-daily with no prior dose escalation—two times the strength of the drug in HERO—demonstrated echocardiographic abnormalities that could be indicative of compromised heart efficiency, the company disclosed in its full-year 2025 report in March. Aardvark ran the healthy-volunteer study as part of a “routine additional cardiac safety” assessment to support a planned regulatory filing, the biotech noted.
The FDA placed HERO and the OLE study under a full clinical hold in May. In August, Aardvark said it had unblinded both studies and no longer plans “resume these trials as previously designed.”

Aardvark subsequently ran a “thorough” ECG study in additional healthy volunteers, which revealed no cardiac events when ARD-101 was dosed at 200 mg and 400 mg twice-a-day, according to the Thursday announcement. The biotech also conducted an in vitro cardiac sodium channel (NaV1.5) study.
ARD-101’s suspension has had wide-ranging consequences for Aardvark. In March, shortly after the initial announcement of the voluntary hold, the company also paused the Phase 2 POWER and STRENGTH studies of ARD-201, an asset that combines ARD-101 with a DPP-4 inhibitor and is being tested for obesity.
POWER was designed to test the ability of ARD-201 to help patients keep weight off after GLP-1 treatment, while STRENGTH assessed the additive benefit of ARD-201 when given alongside GLP-1s. Both continue to be listed on Aardvark’s website. The spokesperson declined to provide comments on ARD-201’s current status.
In the wake of these trial pauses, the biotech laid off employees. From 40 employees and 35 consultants at the end of April, Aardvark’s team had shrunk to 28 employees and 27 consultants by July 31. The workforce reduction was revealed in August.
As of June 30, Aardvark had $73.9 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. The biotech expects this money to “be sufficient to fund operations through the meeting with the FDA to align on Phase 3 plans,” according to the spokesperson.
PWS is a rare and genetic disorder characterized by hyperphagia—the inability to feel full or satisfied, driving a strong urge to keep on eating. Patients with PWS suffer from obesity and related diseases. ARD-101 is designed to activate certain taste receptors in the intestine, especially those that mediate bitterness. This targeting profile leads to the secretion of gut hormones, including GLP-1, to help suppress hunger.
In March 2025, the FDA approved Neurocrine Biosciences’ Vykat XR for the treatment of hyperphagia in PWS. The drug was originally developed by Soleno Therapeutics, which was acquired by Neurocrine for $2.9 billion in April. But it hasn’t been smooth sailing for Neurocrine. A group of doctors in August flagged seven deaths in patients who had taken Vykat XR. Neurocrine is working with the FDA, patient groups and prescribers for a post-marketing surveillance program for patients taking the drug, a spokesperson told BioSpace at the time.

Gold Royalty Chairman and CEO David Garofalo last month at the Mining Forum Americas in Colorado.
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 23, 2026
Gold Royalty (NYSE: GROY) aims to use growing income from its existing portfolio to finance acquisitions without fresh share sales, Chairman and CEO David Garofalo says.
Ten assets now generate income for the company, a number Garofalo expects to double by the end of the decade. The ramp-up of Côté Gold in Ontario and the Vareš mine in Bosnia has helped lift revenue, while new production from Ren in Nevada and the Odyssey underground expansion in Quebec is expected to support further growth.
“Sometimes it can be a year and a half between deals because we do not want to overpay for deals,” Garofalo told The Northern Miner late last month in Colorado Springs. “We don’t want to undermine that per-share value creation that we already have embedded in our portfolio by doing a deal that destroys capital.”
The strategy gives Gold Royalty room to wait in a competitive acquisition market. Mine operators fund construction, exploration and expansions, allowing the royalty holder to benefit from increased output without paying those development costs. Garofalo plans to combine bank borrowing with cash generated by the business to fund purchases and says regular capital returns to shareholders are under active consideration.

Five manufacturers have announced new or expanded U.S. production facilities representing more than $1.6 billion in investments.
The investments highlighted continued spending on domestic manufacturing , transportation equipment and consumer goods.
The projects, located in Texas, Illinois, Georgia, Kentucky and Arkansas, include new manufacturing operations for commercial trailers , school buses, commercial cooling systems and bottled beverages.
Hyundai Translead, Carrier Global Corp. and Blue Bird Corp. account for more than $1.5 billion in announced investments and a combined 5,625 planned jobs.
For trucking companies and logistics providers, the projects could eventually generate a dditional inbound shipments of raw materials and components , as well as outbound movements of finished goods.
The announcements include both projects still in development and recently opened factories.
Hyundai Translead boosts Illinois investment to $600 million
Commercial trailer manufacturer Hyundai Translead announced Thursday that it is increasing its planned investment in two manufacturing facilities in Will County, Illinois, to $600 million, up from the more than $450 million announced in March.
The company also raised its job creation commitment from 2,500 to 3,750 full-time positions.
The additional $150 million investment will support a third production shift and create 1,250 more jobs than originally planned.
Hyundai Translead said the expansion reflects growing customer interest in its Illinois operations and will provide additional manufacturing capacity as the transportation industry recovers.
Hyundai Translead manufactures commercial transportation equipment, including dry van and refrigerated trailers, truck bodies and flatbeds.
The company did not specify which product lines would be manufactured at the Illinois facilities.
Carrier plans $600 million manufacturing center in Fort Worth
Carrier Global Corp. announced Thursday that it will invest more than $600 million over the next three years to establish an advanced manufacturing and engineering center in Fort Worth, Texas.
The project will create 1,500 jobs and occupy more than 1 million square feet at AllianceTexas, a major industrial and logistics development in the Dallas-Fort Worth region.
Carrier (NYSE: CARR ) expects the facility to begin operations in 2027.
The plant will manufacture advanced thermal management systems, including air-cooled and water-cooled commercial chillers used in data centers, hospitals, schools and industrial facilities.
Carrier said the investment responds to strong demand for energy-efficient cooling systems and a record backlog in its commercial heating, ventilation and air conditioning business.
The new facility will also include engineering laboratories and workforce development programs.
Blue Bird announces $300 million Georgia school bus factory
School bus manufacturer Blue Bird Corp. (Nasdaq: BLBD ) plans to invest approximately $300 million in a new manufacturing facility in Fort Valley, Georgia, creating 375 jobs over the next three years.
The company will convert a former diesel-powered motorhome manufacturing site at 401 Wanderlodge Way into a 1-million-square-foot school bus production facility .
Construction is scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027.
The plant will manufacture Type C school buses powered by diesel, gasoline, propane and electricity.
Blue Bird, which was founded in 1927, currently employs more than 1,900 people in Georgia.
Niagara Bottling opens $141 million Kentucky beverage plant
Niagara Bottling celebrated the grand opening Thursday of its new $141 million beverage manufacturing facility in Elsmere, Kentucky.
The 436,000-square-foot facility is located at the C5 Airport East Logistics Center in Kenton County and includes beverage production and distribution operations.
The project will create 60 full-time jobs.
Initially announced in September 2024, the investment has grown by more than $11 million from its original estimate.
Construction began in early 2025 on the 52-acre property developed by CORE5 Industrial Partners.
Niagara Bottling produces bottled water and other beverages for retailers and consumer brands, including sparkling water, flavored water, sports drinks and ready-to-drink beverages.
Primo Brands opens new Arkansas bottled water factory
Primo Brands (NYSE: PRMB ) opened a new manufacturing facility Oct. 14 in Hot Springs, Arkansas, aiming to increase production of its Mountain Valley premium spring water brand.
The 200,000-square-foot factory is the company’s first new manufacturing facility since Primo Brands was formed through a merger in 2024.
The company described the project as a multimillion-dollar investment but did not disclose an exact amount.
The facility includes a high-speed retail production line, two large-format production lines and dedicated logistics and warehouse space. The plant will produce Mountain Valley spring and sparkling water.
Primo Brands said the expansion responds to increasing demand for premium bottled water.
The facility’s additional warehouse and logistics capacity will support distribution of the brand’s products to retailers, restaurants and consumers nationwide.
The company did not disclose the number of jobs created by the project.

Source Rivian
Rivian wants to rebuild the roads its customers drive as 3D test worlds for its self-driving system, and it just bought a 15-person UK startup called Third Dimension to do it, as first reported by TechCrunch .
The startup was founded in 2024 by a former Tesla Autopilot simulation engineer and a veteran of Wayve’s neural simulator team. Rivian didn’t say what it paid.
A video game tool, repurposed
Third Dimension pitched itself as a generative AI tool that builds 3D environments ready for game engines. When it raised a $7 million seed round led by Felicis in October 2024, its target customers were game studios, film, the US military, and autonomous vehicle companies.
The founders’ résumés tell you which of those Rivian cared about. CEO Tolga Kart spent more than two years at Tesla working on Autopilot simulation, after five years as a senior director on Call of Duty at Activision, and later ran engineering at synthetic data company Parallel Domain. Cofounder Piotr Sokólski spent four years at Wayve building photorealistic neural simulators for self-driving cars.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The whole team joins Rivian’s autonomy and AI group under James Philbin. Most of them are in the UK, so Rivian also gets a bigger footprint in London.
“Simulation is central to how we train and validate our autonomous driving systems,” Philbin told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview. He added that Third Dimension “has built impressive technology that turns real-world data into detailed 3D environments.”
400,000 clips a day, few edge cases
Rivian pulls driving footage from R1S, R1T, R2, and commercial van owners who opt into camera data sharing. Philbin told TechCrunch the fleet sends back more than 400,000 sequences every day.
But the vast majority of that footage is boring. The events that actually break self-driving systems, like a mattress in the fast lane, a cop waving traffic through a red light, or a kid running out between parked cars, are rare. You can wait months for your fleet to catch enough of them, or you can rebuild real scenes in 3D and change the variables yourself. That’s the pitch here.
Rivian isn’t first. Waymo unveiled its Waymo World Model , built on Google DeepMind’s Genie 3, back in February to generate scenarios its cars have never seen. Tesla has shown off its own neural “world simulator” for FSD as well.
The Uber clock is running
Rivian needs this to work fast. Uber agreed in March to invest up to $1.25 billion in Rivian to deploy R2 robotaxis , but only $300 million comes up front. The rest is tied to autonomy milestones, starting with 10,000 driverless R2s on Uber’s network in San Francisco and Miami from 2028.
On the consumer side, the timeline has already slipped once. Rivian’s point-to-point driving feature goes to a small group of invited Autonomy+ owners later this year, and those testers have to sign an NDA . “Eyes-off” driving, which RJ Scaringe promised for 2026 back in January 2025, is now a 2027 target, with Level 4 planned for 2028 on the Gen 3 hardware Rivian showed at its AI & Autonomy Day .
Electrek’s Take
We don’t have all the details, but this looks like a good deal. It’s small and targeted, and it buys a team that has already done this exact work at Tesla and Wayve. For a company with a fraction of Tesla’s fleet, getting more out of every clip it collects is the right bet, and Waymo going down the same road tells you the leaders agree.
But simulation is a training and testing tool. It isn’t proof. A system can ace millions of generated edge cases and still screw up on a real street, and the only way the public finds out how it’s actually doing is when the company shares real-world numbers.
However, this is the best way to do a “simulation” because it doesn’t create a fake world with simulated physics; it reconstructs a real-world scene based on real-world data. It’s still a simulation and not as good as the real thing, but it’s as close as it gets.

The disclosure—which came ahead of a presentation of data from the Phase 1 Breakfree-2 study at the ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting—follows Bristol Myers Squibb’s late summer revelation that it had paused certain trials of zolacabtagene autoleucel.
In late August, Bristol Myers Squibb disclosed it had voluntarily paused some autoimmune trials of its CAR T cell therapy zolacabtagene autoleucel after identifying safety signals. Now, BMS has revealed that a death occurred in a Phase 1 study of the candidate in autoimmune disease.
After the data cutoff, one patient with highly active relapsing MS (haRMS) experienced septic pneumonia, which proved fatal, according to BMS’ press release . After infusion of the cell therapy, the patient experienced late onset, non-immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) motor symptoms, BMS said. This was not able to be resolved by treatment with intermittent corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and the patient died the day after developing the pneumonia and 44 days after the infusion of zola-cel.
No additional deaths have been reported “across all zola-cel programs in autoimmune diseases,” BMS added, which include 190 patients treated in Phase 1 studies.
In the Breakfree-2 trial, which included patients with various forms of multiple sclerosis or refractory myasthenia gravis, 42.4% of participants—28 of 66 total—experienced cytokine release syndrome (CRS) events, a common safety issue with cell therapies. Of these cases, 36.4% were deemed Grade 1 and 6.1% were Grade 2 (mild), while all resolved in a median of two days, according to the press release. Beyond the one patient death, one other patient suffered a life-threatening ICANS event that was managed with corticosteroids and anakinra—a biologic drug that helps with the pain and swelling of arthritis—and resolved within four days.
The Breakfree-2 study’s primary endpoint was safety, with efficacy as a secondary measure.
The trial showed “early and promising efficacy” across patients with haRMS and progressive forms of MS (PMS), with all patients treated at dose level 2. At last follow up, all patients treated at this dose level remained off of disease-modifying therapies, including nine patients who had been followed for more than 12 months.

While the United States has one of the largest RV and camper scenes in the world, there are other countries that produce some very capable options. Today, we travel to Ukraine where we find a completely autonomous camper, ‘autonomous’ in the sense that you can indulge in total off-grid living and even light off-road use.
It’s called the X-Rid, no “G,” and currently, it stands as LifeStyle Camper’s total off-grid camping solution. As such, I felt it would be a great idea to run through this beast and see what it has in store for us.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper First and foremost, allow me to point out that the X-Rid is said to start off at around €29,000, or around $32,500, so quite a hefty price by RV standards all around the world. I mean, in the US, you can unlock a camper that has room for as many as eight people at half that price. Still, there are clear reasons why the X-Rid is priced as such.
One of the most important reasons isn’t necessarily the off-grid and off-road systems in place – we'll get to those – but rather, how the shell is built. According to the manufacturer’s website, we’re looking at a composite and self-supporting body composed of sandwich panels with foam core.
While the manufacturer doesn’t make a mention of it, it appears that aluminum extrusions are used to hold those panels in place. If you look closely at the images in the gallery, you can see the edges that line the body
Photo: LifeStyle Camper But, on top of it all, LifeStyle adds a layer of bed liner, enclosing the entire shell in a waterproof and seamless coat. This, however, does not mean that this one is bulletproof in any way; the seams created by windows, cargo bay hatches, the rear door that encloses the kitchen, and any vents or AC units do need to be checked on regularly.
That shell is then placed on top of a steel chassis with running gear provided by Knott, a big name over in Europe, and providing an independent suspension setup with springs and shocks. It’s rated for a peak of 1,500 kg (3,307 lbs) and a standard X-Rid can weigh as little as 1,000 kg (2,205 lbs).
Some wood does make it into the X-Rid, but from what I can see it’s all hidden underneath the panels and inside the camper, so it’s safe from the elements in case the weather takes a turn for the worst. While moisture can be an issue inside campers, the X-Rid is rocking ample vents and windows to keep it dry.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper What I liked about the X-Rid is that it is a camper that is a bit different than most others out there, even though it houses a galley at the rear of this unit, much like a teardrop camper. Inside , LifeStyle adds a modular dinette that transforms into a bed for two guests (comfortably) at night, but the X-Rid is also larger enough to include an en-suite wet bath.
The lifestyle inside is also supported by ample storage along the upper edges of the cabin, a wardrobe across from the bathroom, TV, and curtains to give us some privacy when we wish for it.
Among all that, the manufacturer stuffs this unit full of features to keep us comfortable in the wildest of places. This includes ducted heating and cooling, but also hot water, Alpine audio system, lighting, ventilation, and most importantly, that off-grid system, granted by the one and only EcoFlow, a brand that has grown to be loved the world over for their systems.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper A Delta 3 Plus power station sits at the center of the abilities, along with two charge controllers and 370 W of solar on the roof.
Back outside, LifeStyle continues to equip the X-Rid with a very well-appointed kitchen, ready with a 70-liter fridge, sink/cooktop combo with flush countertop, ample storage, and a pass-through that allows the interior and kitchen to communicate with one another. Speakers are also in place to enjoy some tunes while cooking.
Given the size and strength of the X-Rid's body, we can also see an awning sticking off the side, perfect for setting up a little outdoor dining area and lounge – why not grab an annex – and on top, a rack system means we can add plenty of extra cargo. More cargo can be stuffed into the body itself via those hatches we see.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper Keep in mind that this is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of what the X-Rid has in store and just how much more it can be decked out in options and extras. This means that, if you’re in Europe and like what you see here, be sure to get in touch with LifeStyle for the full tour of their freshest camper.
If, however, you live in the US or anywhere other than Europe, you may have a very hard time getting your hands on this one. But, if you like what you see, at least you’ll know what to look for locally.

source_document.body:
Four and a half years after a grassroots union was voted in by workers at an Amazon warehouse in Staten Island, New York, the battles in court over Amazon’s pushback against the vote continues.
At issue in the latest set of filings in the Fifth Circuit is a National Labor Relations Board decision from April where the NLRB ordered Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) to negotiate with the union, which after its successful vote to unionize with no particular national organization is now aligned with the Teamsters as ALU-International Brotherhood of Teamsters (IBT) Local 1, with the ALU standing for Amazon Labor Union .
There were dual filings last week with the Fifth Circuit in the case of Amazon vs. NLRB over the board’s April decision to require Amazon to sit down and bargain with the Teamsters for a contract covering the workers at the facility known as JFK8.
The briefs filed October 16 by Amazon and the Teamsters are vastly different, not just because they are coming at the case as adversaries, but because they take an entirely different approach.
Legal arguments by Amazon
The Amazon brief is more on narrow legal grounds about what the NLRB can and can not do.
The Teamsters brief is a 115-page behemoth that relitigates and reviews the entire history of the Staten Island union and the many of the disputes that have been a hallmark of the contentious relationship between the Teamsters and Amazon.
For Amazon, the battle on Staten Island marks the only time it has ever faced off against a unionization drive at one of its facilities and lost.
For example, a year later, another attempt at unionization at a separate Staten Island facility failed.
In a closely-watched 2021 election because it was the first of a kind, Amazon beat back a unionization drive at its facility in Bessemer, Alabama. In that case it was not the Teamsters but the Retail, Wholesale and Department Store Workers Union that sought to represent workers there.
Oral arguments…or not
In the Fifth Circuit case, the two sides are far enough apart that their respective briefs couldn’t even agree on whether there is a need for oral arguments.
“While this Court could deny Amazon’s petition for review and grant the Board’s motion for enforcement without oral argument, the Court may find oral argument useful to address the briefing,” the union said in a fence-straddling statement in its brief.
What did Amazon say? “Amazon agrees with (the union) that the issues raised in its petition can be decided without oral argument.”
Why it didn’t bargain
The Amazon brief is notable also in that it says it has not bargained with the union because it was seeking a court to overturn the NLRB’s certification of the election and the April order for it to negotiate. A lack of bargaining was needed to push the issue to a court, the company said.
“An employer cannot obtain direct judicial review of a decision certifying a union election,” the Amazon brief says. “Instead, the employer must refuse to bargain with the union, be found to have committed an unfair labor practice, and then challenge the certification when it seeks review of that finding.”
The legal term of what Amazon is pursuing in its action against the NLRB is a “test of certification challenge.”
NLRB Edge, a blog about the NLRB written by Matt Bruenig, said in a post following the NLRB decision that the board rejected Amazon’s arguments after “finding that all representation issues raised by Amazon either were or could have been litigated in the underlying representation proceeding, and that Amazon offered no newly discovered evidence or special circumstances justifying reconsideration.”
Was it a big win?
Amazon’s brief does touch on allegations it has leveled against the union. It said the union’s Staten Island efforts “engaged in a campaign marked by threats, coercion and intimidation.” It also said the union “narrowly prevailed” in its election; by contrast, the union touted the win as being a margin of almost 11% of all ballots cast.
But the more legally-oriented question the Amazon action against the NLRB puts before the Fifth Circuit is focused on a union request that beyond just ordering Amazon to bargain, it must engage in an “enhanced remedy.” The union describes the remedy as Amazon reading aloud at a “mandatory meeting”, according to the union, “a notice of employees’ rights under the National Labor Relations Act.”
Although such a reading had been recommended by the NLRB’s General Counsel, the full board rejected that remedy.
Amazon is recommending rejection of that union request because, one, it thinks the election on Staten Island is going to be decertified, making the issue moot.
Second, the “enhanced remedy” of the reading of rights in a test-of-certification case has no precedent in labor law, according to Amazon.
And third, Amazon says the union has not made a sufficient case that the reading is warranted.
The union says if the Fifth Circuit agrees with Amazon’s arguments, “it would be improper to set aside the election.” Instead, it recommends the case be remanded to the NLRB “to provide further rationale for its decision.”
Joint employer case rolls on
Meanwhile, another battle between the Teamsters and Amazon continues to play out before the NLRB.
The fight there is over an April agreement between Amazon and the NLRB’s General Counsel . That agreement was designed to end a process on terms favorable to Amazon in which a lower rung of the NLRB process in Los Angeles had found that Amazon was a joint employer along with a direct service provider, the independently-owned companies that actually deliver products.
That agreement stopped the process that was launched in Los Angeles from getting to the full board.
Amazon has long argued that its DSPs are independent. The Teamsters have argued otherwise and that Amazon is a joint employer with all of them, given their level of control over the delivery companies. It isn’t a stretch to say that in terms of its labor structure, being held to be a joint employer would be almost an existential threat to the way it does business.
The deal struck by the General Counsel ending the process was favorable enough to Amazon that Teamsters lawyers at the time called it an “ambush settlement agreement.”
The NLRB docket on the case has mostly been quiet in recent months. The last substantive entry on it is a letter from Teamsters attorneys who said that unless there is an “immediate reinstatement of these proceedings,” accepting the agreement “will represent the Board’s capitulation to the corporate interests that operate to the detriment of working people across the country, who depend on the Board to effectuate the Act and protect their rights.”

A combination of Tango Therapeutics’ vopimetostat and Revolution Medicines’ recently approved Rasonque led to a response rate of 82% in an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial—a drop from 92% that was reported in June in fewer patients.
Tango Therapeutics was trading down on Friday after updated results from a mid-stage study of its pancreatic cancer candidate combined with Revolution Medicines’ recently approved Rasonque showed a lower response rate than previously reported.
Tango announced updated results from the ongoing Phase 1/2 study of its investigational PRMT5 inhibitor vopimetostat combined with daraxonrasib— greenlit by the FDA as Rasonque for second-line pancreatic cancer—that show an 82% objective response rate in 22 evaluable patients. Median progression-free survival (PFS) has not yet been reached in the study, but PFS was 88% in patients with second- or third-line pancreatic cancer, Tango said. The data will be presented this weekend at the European Society of Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid.

The FDA granted the approval of Revolution Medicines’ daraxonrasib, now to be known as Rasonque, in pancreatic adenocarcinoma 6.5 months ahead of deadline.

Tango previously revealed data in June from 12 patients in the trial, showing a 92% response rate and PFS of 90% at six months. The results received much fanfare.
“WOW!” Leerink Partners wrote in a note to investors at the time, predicting the biotech’s stock would at least double on the data. Sure enough, shares of Tango rose 43% at market open on June 8 to $28.94. As of publication on Friday, the company was down nearly 18% from the previous day’s close, trading at $22.91.
Analysts, however, did not appear too concerned with the less-stunning results. The updated data are “supportive of the highly synergistic effect of the combination,” William Blair analysts said in a Thursday note.
The data met Jefferies’ expectations, with the analysts expressing confidence in a Thursday note that the response rate would reach or exceed 70%—a bar the combo more than cleared.
As for safety, the combination was generally well-tolerated in 25 patients with pancreatic cancer or non-small cell lung cancer who received dose level 1— 200 mg of vopimetostat and 600 mg of daraxonrasib every day—with no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). Dose level 2— 250 mg and 600 mg, respectively, “was not well-tolerated,” according to Tango’s release, with three of four patients experiencing DLTs.
Tango plans to seek the FDA’s guidance regarding a possible accelerated approval path for vopimetostat plus daraxonrasib in the second-line pancreatic cancer setting, Tango CEO Malte Peters said during a Friday morning conference call to discuss the data.
Tango also plans to launch a Phase 3 trial of the combo in patients with front-line (1L) pancreatic cancer with MTAP deletions in the first half of 2027, Peters said in a prepared statement on Friday. Approximately 40% of patients with pancreatic cancer have an MTAP deletion, the executive added. The company will move forward with dose level 1 and compare the combination against standard of care chemotherapy.
“It is encouraging to see that the clinical activity and tolerability observed in our initial June 2026 dataset has been confirmed with longer follow-up and in a larger patient population, affirming our belief that the response rate and durability observed with vopimetostat plus daraxonrasib surpass any published PDAC [pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma] datasets, even in front-line settings,” Peters said.
Notably, William Blair said that “it is too difficult to draw real conclusions on the 1L trend,” with only two evaluable patients—one of whom did not respond to the combo.
RevMed is also looking to move Rasonque into the first line setting for pancreatic cancer. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the drug in that setting in September, weeks after its second-line approval. The designation was based on data from patients with treatment-naive RAS mutant metastatic pancreatic cancer treated with RevMed’s drug in the open-label Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 trial. In this study, daraxonrasib combined with a standard of care chemotherapy regimen showed “encouraging preliminary antitumor activity” and a manageable safety profile, according to the biotech’s announcement.
The ongoing RASolute 303 trial is now studying daraxonrasib as a monotherapy and in combination with this chemo regimen versus chemotherapy alone in patients with previously untreated metastatic PDAC.
On Tango’s call Friday morning, Peters said that “executing against our pivotal study in frontline pancreatic cancer is our primary goal.” He added that the biotech aims for vopimetastat to become “a PRMT5 combination partner of choice for any RAS inhibitor.”
To achieve the goal, Tango is deprioritizing novel target discovery, according to a Friday SEC filing . The company intends to reduce its workforce by 14%, “with the majority of the headcount reductions from the company’s research group.”
Tango had 97 R&D employees and 137 full-time staffers in total as of Dec. 31, 2025, per an end-of-year SEC filing , meaning that around 19 people are losing their jobs at the biotech.

KYIV, Ukraine — Washington blamed Moscow at the United Nations on Wednesday for deliberately moving a Russian military satellite with an undisclosed mission “dangerously” close last week to a U.S.-registered satellite believed to serve Ukraine, with officials vowing to defend American interests in space.
The Russian satellite, Cosmos 2612, spent more than two weeks maneuvering toward ICEYE-X36, a radar satellite operated by the American arm of Finnish company ICEYE that supplies imagery to Ukraine’s military through some of its spacecraft, then shadowed it from as close as a third of a mile through the weekend of Oct. 17.
U.S. Undersecretary of State Thomas G. DiNanno called the Russian satellite’s behavior “threatening,” and said the country had been “intentionally maneuvering dangerously close to a commercial satellite, behaviors consistent with on-orbit weapons operations.”
Space historian and former NASA astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell said that he believed it is the first rendezvous in low Earth orbit between two active satellites without one owner’s approval.
The close encounter came weeks after Air Force Secretary Troy Meink publicly confirmed that the U.S. has weapons in orbit and the Space Force picked two companies to build space-to-space reconnaissance satellites . It also followed reports that trillionaire Elon Musk — under White House orders — slowed the military-grade Starlink that Ukraine relies on, rendering some of the country’s essential air defense weapons useless.
The operation fits a wider Russian campaign of intimidation against Europe and the U.S. that lets Russian President Vladimir Putin “poke the West in the eye and watch the West do nothing,” according to Clayton Swope, deputy director of the Aerospace Security Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
“They prove a point – the West can’t stop me,” Swope added Wednesday during a CSIS panel on the encounter.
As the U.S. and its allies increasingly rely on commercial capabilities for national security, key assets like satellites have “become vulnerabilities that can be exploited by our adversary,” according to Greg Gillinger, senior vice president of strategy and development at Virginia-based Integrity ISR, who also spoke on the CSIS panel.
The impact of a possible satellite attack could reach well beyond one company or country, since commercial satellites now carry much of the imagery and connectivity militaries fight with, experts said. Musk’s Starlink slowdown in Ukraine showed how quickly a military force can suffer when that access is throttled without notice — and how easily local geopolitical conflicts can explode into global security crises.
On Oct. 12, commercial trackers feeding the U.S. military’s Joint Commercial Operations cell flagged the possible rendezvous when Cosmos 2612 slid into ICEYE-X36’s orbit roughly 345 miles above Earth, according to Integrity ISR’s newsletter .
On Oct. 15 and 16, the Russian satellite moved from more than 200 miles behind ICEYE-X36 to roughly 3 miles away before moving in closer and holding position through the weekend, tracking firm LeoLabs said in a statement reported by CNN .
Both satellites travel at roughly 4 miles (7 kilometers) per second, so getting two objects “within a hundred meters or even a kilometer” of each other is “the equivalent of flying in a very tight formation in an aircraft,” Gillinger said.
“Russia didn’t accidentally get within a kilometer of X36,” he said. “It is an indication of intent that they’re sending a message.”
ICEYE, whose radar satellites see through clouds, smoke and darkness, expanded cooperation with Ukraine’s military, pledging continued imagery “on tactical timelines,” according to a January statement . However, the company has not confirmed which of its satellites serve Kyiv.
Moscow has warned since the first year of its full-scale invasion that Western commercial satellites helping Ukraine could become legitimate military targets.
ICEYE said it is “aware of the situation and tracking it closely” and that its “constellation architecture is designed for continuity and resilience,” a spokesperson told Air & Space Forces Magazine earlier this week.
Russia’s intent behind the satellite maneuvers remains unclear. According to LeoLabs, an American space technology company, possible aims range from intelligence collection and close inspection to coercion and groundwork for future operations against satellites.
The maneuvers demonstrated capabilities that could be used to “inspect, characterize, shadow, or potentially interfere with another spacecraft,” though they “do not establish hostile intent,” the company said.
Analysts could not yet say whether Moscow planned an attack and then reversed course, or was orbiting nearby for another purpose entirely.
Russia could have been doing “a dry run” for a future attack, or the satellite could have been carrying a weapon, from a jammer to a laser to a projectile, Swope explained.
“Was the intent to blow up the satellite? No,” he said. “Was the intent to put some type of energy on the satellite? Probably… I don’t know why you’d need to maneuver in this way, this close, unless you wanted to do something that involved putting energy on that satellite.”
The Russian satellite has since pulled back, but not far.
It was again flying at ICEYE-X36’s altitude on Wednesday, holding roughly 250 miles (400 kilometers) behind it, and could “easily close that gap again at the time and place of their choosing,” Gillinger said.
Russia could try to approach another ICEYE satellite within weeks, as two more satellites from the same launch will soon line up with the orbit of a second satellite, ICEYE-X37, according to Integrity ISR.
If they move in, “we could see another scenario where another commercial satellite is closely trailed by one of these Russian satellites,” Gillinger said.
The retreat began Oct. 18, two days after President Donald Trump signed an executive order waiving tariffs and most economic restrictions on Russia.
Swope said Trump’s move to ease sanctions “could have been a reason why Putin said, ‘You know, now’s not the time to exacerbate tensions specifically with the United States. Maybe we should pause this operation.’”
“If you’re getting close to a deal on something, why jeopardize that?” he said.
The potential for a conflict in space has been growing in recent months.
Washington “appears to lack response options” if Russia threatened U.S. military and commercial satellites with a nuclear weapon in orbit, according to the conclusions from a 2025 war-game scenario where fictional Russian space objects threatened American interests.
There is no public indication that Cosmos 2612 carries a nuclear weapon, but Swope said that there is also still no internationally recognized rule for determining if a maneuver like this one should be considered hostile — or what international standards should be followed in a response.
“Even though we all can make a good case on why this was [hostile], there’s no norm that you could point to,” he said.
Without a clear response plan or real consequences for aggression, menacing satellite moves like this one are “literally just a spigot that Russia could turn on and off” to increase pressure on adversaries, Swope said.
Russia, he added, “is going to turn it on again.”

Retaliation Threatened if the UK Joins EU Tariffs on Chinese Electric Vehicles
28 photos
Photo: Lepas
Asia's most economically powerful nation shipped 255,000 vehicles to the United Kingdom in the first half of 2026. That's 87 percent year over year, and just around 181,000 of those vehicles were optioned with electrified powertrains. Just like Europe, the showrooms in Britain are becoming an increasingly useful outlet for Chinese newcomers.
London, however, finds itself between a rock and a hard place. Beijing has recently issued a warning, with the Ministry of Commerce threatening countermeasures if the United Kingdom imposes EU-style tariffs on Chinese-built electric vehicles. The ministry told Britain to avoid simply following the EU's lead, think twice, and follow the World Trade Organization rules.
The trigger? That came from UK trade minister Anas Sarwar, who said that Britain and the European Union should act in lockstep to address the People's Republic of China's growing influence. Sarwar also made it clear that London was discussing potential tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles with European partners.
A policy change hasn't been announced, which is why China's response could very well be considered an overreaction. After all, Chinese automakers rely on exports as domestic electric vehicle demand continues to cool down amid intense price competition and fading subsidies. Furthermore, extended-range electric vehicles are getting increasingly popular with Chinese motorists.
For the time being, as highlighted by Automotive News, the United Kingdom still applies its 10 percent import tariff to China-made vehicles of all types. The EU has added specific duties aimed at Chinese battery-electric vehicles, and you are correct to view those duties as a protectionist response.
Photo: Lepas The dispute is tied to a larger negotiation over industrial policy, with Britain eager to join the EU's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act. Proposed by the European Commission in March 2026, this act's main targets are boosting domestic manufacturing while enhancing supply chain resilience. Simply put, said act favors Euro-made products for very sensible reasons.
A Franco-German proposal would enable Britain's participation, but with a catch. That catch is to align with EU trade defense measures. The legislation remains under negotiation as of this writing. The alignment condition would pull British trade policy much closer to Brussels than London might otherwise choose.
As a case in point, the EU imposed additional countervailing duties of up to 35.3 percent on Chinese battery-electric vehicles. Add the standard 10 percent levy to that, and you get a maximum combined rate of 45.3 percent. If Britain were to follow suit, Chinese automakers would be greatly hindered by said tariffs.
Speaking of alignment, the European Commission plans an annual cap of 350,000 Chinese hybrid vehicles from December 2026, reducing China's share of the EU hybrid passenger vehicle market from 6 to 3 percent. Britain's participation would also hurt China, hence the ministry's rather aggressive reaction.
As it stands, China wants the UK to understand that trade restrictions come with consequences outside the automotive industry. While it has not named potential targets, China doesn't appear to be bluffing here. As for the UK, post-Brexit woes could very well be the catalyst for playing ball with the EU.

Barzan Holdings' unmanned surface vessel unveiled at DIMDEX 2026 (Breaking Defense/ Agnes Helou)
BEIRUT — As Qatar steps up efforts to expand its domestic defense industry, the state-owned company Barzan Holdings unveiled more than a dozen defense platforms at the Milipol 2026 exhibition in Doha this week.
The new systems include first-person-view (FPV) drones, vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) uncrewed aerial vehicles, unmanned surface vessels and electronic warfare platforms.
“This is a significant achievement, particularly as we continue to expand Qatar’s domestic defence and security capabilities in a year where we have had to rise to a number of regional challenges,” the company said in a statement.
According to information provided by the firm, Barzan displayed several FPV and VTOL drones for the first time, including:
FPV Drone-15 inch: A tactical reconnaissance quadcopter with a payload capacity of up to 4 kilograms (8.8 pounds), a range of 20 kilometers and an endurance of up to 20 minutes.
FPV Drone-10 inch: A tactical reconnaissance quadcopter capable of carrying up to 2.5 kilograms (5.5 pounds), with a range of 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) and an endurance of 12 minutes at full payload.
FPV Drone-7 inch: A rapid-deployment quadcopter capable carrying 1.5 kilograms (3.3 pounds), with a range of 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) and an endurance of up to 15 minutes.
H Silent ISR Quadcopter: A multirotor drone equipped with an electro-optical and infra red gimbal. It features an endurance of up to 40 minutes and a datalink range of 40 kilometers (24.8 miles), and is designed for surveillance, border security and critical infrastructure protection.
ISR VTOL-400: A vertical take-off and landing UAV with a 4 kilogram (8.8 pounds) payload capacity, datalink range of 40 kilometers (24.8 miles), maximum operating altitude of 10,000 feet and speed of 110 kilometers per hour (68.3 miles per hour).
Barzan also unveiled two unmanned surface vessels during the exhibition. The first, the Rasid USV, is an unmanned jet ski-style watercraft capable of performing surveillance missions. The second, the Barzan Conversion Solution, is a coast guard vessel that can operate either manned or unmanned.
In the communications sector, Barzan introduced Secure Comms VPN and Secure Comms CHAT, designed to support secure communications and protect users’ privacy, according to the statement.
The new systems underscore the country’s push to grow its defense industry under the “Made in Qatar” initiative, as Doha faces growing pressure to strengthen its ability to protect critical infrastructure and counter aerial threats following Iranian missile and drone attacks. Like other Gulf states , Qatar was targeted by Iranian missiles and drones, and it was the only Gulf state struck by an Israeli raid in September 2025.
During the Milipol exhibition, Barzan also announced a joint venture with Ukrainian company Carmine Sky to develop a layered “Full-­Cycle Air Defence” capability, aimed at meeting sovereign and national security requirements and protecting critical assets, according to Barzan.
The joint venture will allow Doha to leverage Ukraine’s expertise to deliver an integrated, layered air defense architecture that combines detection, identification and neutralization capabilities, Barzan said. The system is expected to counter a range of unmanned aerial vehicles — from FPV drones to jet-powered UAVs — and incorporate radar, radio-frequency sensors, electronic warfare systems and hard-kill platforms.

Workstation
MSI XpertStation WS300 Front Hero
Today we are looking at our second NVIDIA DGX Station-powered system with MSI’s XpertStation WS300. These NVIDIA GB300-based systems bring NVIDIA’s server-grade hardware to a desk-side computer for the first time, letting developers and other workstation users test and run programs in a local AI setting. With a 1.6kW maximum power draw and an extensive liquid cooling system, these DGX Station systems pack as much server hardware as you can fit into a desktop tower, and even then, only barely.
Last month we looked at our first DGX Station system with Gigabyte’s W775-V10-L01 . You may have seen that in that review, and in this one, we took the opportunity to network two systems using the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC for an 800Gbps aggregate Blackwell Ultra-to-Blackwell Ultra RDMA link. Unlike many pre-AI-era workstations where networking was an afterthought, here MSI and NVIDIA are making it central to scaling to service more users and larger models. It also features an expansive closed-loop liquid cooling system to keep all that hardware cool. As a result, this system not only delivers strong performance, but it also has a lot going on under the hood to enable it.
MSI XpertStation WS300 Key Specs
CPU | NVIDIA Grace 72-Core Neoverse V2 (72C/72T)
GPU | NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra
Operating System | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with NVIDIA AI Developer Tools
Memory | CPU: 496GB LPDDR5X (396GB/s) GPU: 252GB HBM3E (7.1TB/s)
Storage | 2x M.2 2280 (PCIe Gen6 x4) 2x M.2 2280 (PCIe Gen5 x4)
Video Card | Optional: NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell 2000/4000/6000
PSU | 1600W (80 PLUS Platinum)
Form Factor | Tower Workstation 246 x 529 x 570 mm (9.67 x 20.83 x 22.46 in)
Networking | 2x 400Gbps (QSFP112, ConnectX-8) 10Gb Ethernet (RJ45, Marvell) 1Gb Ethernet (BMC)
Ports | Top: 2x USB-C 10Gbps, 2x USB-A 10Gbps, 1x 3.5mm Line-Out, 1x 3.5mm Mic-In Rear: 4x USB-A 10Gbps, 1x USB Micro-B UART (BMC), 2x 400GbE (QSFP112), 1x 10GbE LAN (RJ45, Marvell), 1x 1GbE LAN (RJ45, BMC), 3x 3.5mm Audio, 1x Mini DisplayPort (BMC)
Meanwhile, every DGX Station vendor is putting their own spin on how a GB300 desktop should be built, and MSI is no different. For MSI, that means considering not only the GB300 hardware itself, but also how best to mount a high-end RTX Pro video card inside the system. Consequently, if your GB300 workstation needs a proper graphics adapter to round out the experience, MSI has that process covered.
So without further ado, let us dive right in.
MSI XpertStation WS300 External Hardware Overview
With a combination of very large chips and an extensive liquid cooling system, MSI’s XpertStation WS300 sits in a full-size PC tower case measuring 53cm tall and 57cm deep. If its size alone does not clue you in to how massive this system is, you will quickly feel it when you try to lift it, thanks to its hefty weight of nearly 30kg.
The WS300’s overall design is typical for a desktop workstation. Painted and clad entirely in black, it is clear this is a high-end system of some sort, and one that requires a lot of cooling, but you would be hard-pressed to guess it is a $100K+ system with a server processor set tucked inside. It is an expensive system, but not flashy, unlike what we have seen with NVIDIA’s DGX Spark and the like.
We will cover the cooling system in more detail later in our internal hardware tour, but it is worth noting that the front of this system is open. Behind the triangular mesh screen covering the front of the system are the system’s internals. This is a stark difference from Gigabyte’s DGX Station system, where the front was entirely closed off.
MSI XpertStation WS300-Side 1
With the left side of the system being entirely blank, we will start on the right side of the case. Here we see the back of a radiator, with three fans pushing air through it as part of the system’s extensive liquid cooling.
MSI’s decision to reserve the entire front of the case for airflow means there are no I/O ports or buttons on the front. Given the size, weight, and heat output, MSI designed the WS300 as a floor computer, so it places its ports and controls along the top of the case.
MSI XpertStation WS300-Top 1
For its DGX Station system, MSI offers a decent port selection, though the system is still somewhat held back by the limitations of the GB300 hardware. We find a pair of 10Gbps USB-A ports and a pair of 10Gbps USB-C ports right next to them.
MSI XpertStation WS300-Top I O 1
You will not find any USB4-speed ports on the system. NVIDIA’s DGX Station motherboard provides none. Transfers faster than 10Gbps must go through the system’s massive-throughput dual 400Gb QSFP112 array via the integrated ConnectX-8 SuperNIC. A fair point someone on our team raised is that, technically, you can use the PCIe card slots to add more USB options. However, we think it is better used as a server you connect to over the network.
MSI XpertStation WS300-Reset Button 1
Along with the standard USB ports, MSI’s system also provides dedicated 3.5mm audio input and output ports, and even a green drive activity light, with the HDD symbol amusingly outliving hard drives in workstation systems (GB300 does not provide SATA ports). This is also where we find the system’s somewhat questionable power and reset controls. Towards the front of the system, the WS300’s power button has a green LED to helpfully show system status. Behind that is a rather recessed reset button. Because these controls face up, recessing the reset button helps prevent accidental resets, but it also makes it harder to trigger intentionally, so it has drawbacks.
On the plus side, MSI has done better than others here by labeling their USB ports with the USB-IF logo. It would still be better if they listed the port speeds, especially for the potentially speedy USB-C ports.
MSI XpertStation WS300-Rear Angled 1
Shifting to the rear of the WS300, we find the back side of a standard PC chassis. This means we are looking at the familiar fan, rear I/O, expansion slot, and PSU layout of the ATX form factor. The chassis accepts either a 120mm or 140mm fan for rear exhaust, with MSI opting for a 120mm fan.
MSI XpertStation WS300 Rear IO (Full)
The rear I/O is dominated by networking. As a reminder, DGX Station systems use a standardized NVIDIA motherboard, so all Station systems share the same I/O arrangement here. Including the 1GbE port for the BMC, the WS300 has four Ethernet ports routed to three different controllers.
MSI XpertStation WS300-QSFP112 400G Ethernet Ports 2
Chief among these are the two QSFP112 ports, which are fed by NVIDIA’s powerful ConnectX-8 “SuperNIC”. Each port offers 400Gbps networking and is the primary way the system connects to high-speed storage and/or other DGX Station-based systems. The ConnectX-8 SuperNIC driving these ports does a lot of heavy lifting beyond networking, and the capabilities and limitations of these QSFP ports are somewhat complex as a result (more on this in a bit).
Compared to the Gigabyte system we looked at previously, MSI has put more thought into keeping the QSFP112 cages cool. There is no active airflow here, but the I/O shield does not block it either.
MSI XpertStation WS300-Rear IO 2
For more mundane networking use cases, the system also has a pair of RJ45 Ethernet jacks. The left 1G port connects to the BMC and is for system management. OpenBMC handles management via an HTML5 iKVM. The RJ45 jack on the right side is a 10Gb Ethernet port powered by Marvell’s tried-and-true 10GbE controller. The system topology is fascinating. MSI’s Marvell 10Gbase-T controller is attached to the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC’s built-in PCIe switch, then to the CPU. It does not connect directly to the CPU. We have seen 10G ports connect through PCHs on other platforms, but this is using a high-end SuperNIC.
MSI XpertStation WS300 USB 3.1 Type A Ports 4
Below are the remaining WS300 USB ports. These four ports all run at 10Gbps, matching the speed of the USB ports on the top of the system. These ports are routed through a USB hub, so you should not expect 10Gbps from each one simultaneously.
MSI XpertStation WS300 Rear Audio Jacks
To the right, we have a trio of audio jacks for two-channel audio out, plus separate mic and line-in jacks.
MSI XpertStation WS300 Mini DisplayPort 2
At the end of the rear I/O panel, two more ports connect to the BMC. On the left is a serial UART in a micro-USB form factor. To the right is a Mini DisplayPort output from the BMC for system management and configuration. DGX Station systems do not have a true integrated display GPU (Blackwell Ultra is more of a compute accelerator), so the BMC provides the only out-of-the-box graphics output. For a full-featured graphics solution, you can pair DGX Station systems with a compatible NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell video card. We will discuss that later, but you can look up compatible cards at the time you read this review.
MSI XpertStation WS300-AC Power Input 2
Finally, here is a look at the bottom of the system, where the power supply resides. Thanks in large part to the GB300 accelerator inside each of them, DGX Station systems are extremely power-hungry, and NVIDIA is right at the limit for a single North American power outlet here with their 1600 Watt power supply. The 80 PLUS Platinum-rated PSU needs a high-capacity C19 power cable to safely handle that amperage and a 20-amp circuit to run it. In practice, this system effectively requires its own dedicated 20A circuit.
That is the outside of MSI’s WS300 DGX Station. For the rest of the story, let us dive into the system’s chassis, where this gets very different.

The Chinese auto giant has greatly expanded its portfolio over the past few months and years. BYD now offers everything from entry-level EVs to three-row flagship SUVs, pickup trucks, electric supercars, and just about everything in between.

How would you like to spend $159,000 over MSRP on a brand-new Corvette ZR1X? Tempting, right? I'm only being half-sarcastic, because if you're a collector, this is exactly the type of Corvette you want to buy. A brand-new, limited-edition flagship spec with delivery miles.
Thing is, this is going to be a long-term investment, so make sure you're good with that. Otherwise, you might be disappointed trying to sell this car in a year or two. Prices will go down before going back up again, even on limited edition supercars with hypercar-like performance such as the ZR1X.
Ideally, you'll want to sell this thing in like 2056 and make a few million bucks. Or whatever the equivalent of that will be three decades from now. What will work in your favor, as a collector, is that cars will be completely different in the future. Internal combustion will certainly be extinct 30 years from now, and people will look at the ZR1X the same way we might look at an all-original, numbers-matching, never driven, time capsule Boss 429 in today's market.
But in the meantime, scarcity won't be a factor and you'll have plenty of high performance models catching up to the ZR1X in terms of speed and acceleration. Almost certainly the next-generation C9 Corvette.
Now, about the Quail Silver Limited Edition variant specifically, we saw a nearly identical car back in May that sold for $452,000 with an MSRP of $290,678. That one also had delivery miles. Meanwhile, this one here just sold for $430,000, and its original MSRP was $271,570. Seems pretty fair. Or at least it's within market parameters.
Of course, anyone who's not a collector should avoid this limited edition spec like the plague, because you can get a ZR1X for way less than that. Around $330,000 should do it, on average - if you want it ASAP, that is. Meaning you'd have to win it during auction.
In terms of specs, this example is finished in Blade Silver Matte and comes with the Carbon Fiber Aero package (high-wing rear spoiler, dive planes, hood spoiler). Other visual highlights include the LED headlights, front and rear cameras, silver 20" and 21" forged wheels with Michelin rubber, plus the carbon-ceramic brakes with orange-finished calipers.
Photo: Bring a Trailer There's also a front axle lift system and you get the ZTK Performance suspension for good measure.
Inside is where you'll find the likes of the GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilated), Sky Cool Gray and Medium Ash Gray leather upholstery with Habanero accents, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, head-up display, and a limited edition badge between the seats that identifies this car as build #46 of a reported 100.
As for performance, the twin-turbocharged 5.5L LT7 V8 engine is working alongside an electric motor for a combined output of 1,250 horsepower and 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque. Over a quarter-mile, this is an 8-second car when running at its best.

This 1969 Chevy Impala Hasn't Moved an Inch in 10 Years, Big-Block Surprise Under the Hood

Photo: eBay seller ccca_305
This 1969 Chevrolet Impala hasn’t moved a single inch in the last 10 years. The reason wasn’t shared on eBay, where the owner decided to list the car, but the Impala is now ready to get back into action and return to the road.
The car looks like an easy project, as the issues you can spot in these photos don’t suggest anything that could become a reason to walk away.
Sure, it also depends on your expectations. If you’re particularly interested in an all-original Impala, you’ll have to inspect this car in person because it’s unclear if this is the case. But if you just want a regular driver that you can take out on sunny Sundays, this Impala seems to be a good choice.
Photo: eBay seller ccca_305 Born in 1958 as a Bel Air version and promoted to a stand-alone series a year later, the Impala rapidly became the best-selling Chevrolet. It continued to dominate the brand’s sales throughout the next decade, and the 1969 model year made no difference.
The Impala was still the top full-size Chevrolet , accounting for 777,000 cars of all 1.1 million full-size units built by the GM brand. The Caprice was the runner-up, but the difference was huge: only 166,000 buyers ordered a Caprice. The Bel Air fell to a little over 155,000 cars, while the Biscayne, which continued to be the most affordable full-size Chevrolet, represented only 68,700 orders.
One of the biggest changes that happened in the Impala lineup in 1969 was how Chevrolet offered the Super Sport. No longer being offered as an option or separate series, the Super Sport could only be ordered as part of the Z24 package, which represented the SS 427, available only for the Sport Coupe, the Custom Coupe, and the convertible.
Fitted with a 427ci engine rated at 390 horsepower, the Super Sport could be had for no more, no less than $422.
This wasn’t the most powerful engine in the lineup, though. While Chevrolet continued to offer a six and a 327 as the base engines, the company also wanted to offer as much power as possible for those who wanted to get a boost of adrenaline behind the wheel of an Impala. In addition to the L36, which could also be ordered without the SS treatment for $237, buyers could also get the L72.
This was an upgraded version of the 427, this time rated at 425 horsepower and carrying an extra price (for non-SS buyers) of $447.
Photo: eBay seller ccca_305 This Impala is fitted with the non-SS 427 rated at 335 horsepower, and according to the seller, it still runs great. This is certainly good news, considering the car has been off the road for a while, so my recommendation is that you still ask your mechanic to inspect it in person before you make an offer.
There are things that don’t work on this car, so the time in storage has clearly taken its toll. The hideaway headlights aren’t working despite still being complete.
However, the vehicle is still very solid, at least based on the photos published online. There’s obvious corrosion, but I don’t think this is a critical problem. The images don’t reveal any rot or rust that has gotten through, so the damage is mostly on the surface and should be easy to deal with.
The best thing about this car is that it’s still complete, so even if something is not in its best shape, it should be fixable. Sure, nobody can tell this for sure unless they see the car live, so call the seller and maybe ask for a digital walkaround to see the advertised solid floors and trunk more thoroughly.
Photo: eBay seller ccca_305 The price isn’t necessarily surprising, considering this is a big-block 1969 Chevrolet Impala. An SS would have made it significantly more appealing to full-size Chevrolet fanboys, but at first glance, it still checks many of the right boxes to get a full refresh.
There are questions left without an answer, including regarding the car’s originality. A demanding collector or die-hard Chevy fan would look for the full package, so more information is certainly required for this Impala.
The seller listed the car for auction, with the starting bid set at $28,000. A reserve is also in place, but that’s not necessarily bad news because it’s unlikely to be far from the Buy It Now price, which has been configured at $36,400. This is the price anyone has to pay to get their hands on the car without a fight, though right now, the auction is still at zero bids.
The digital fight should come to an end in 8 days, but if nobody submits an offer, we should see this Impala getting relisted in the coming weeks. The car is parked in East Meadow, New York, and it should be able to move on its own power after it sells.
